description: Initial baseline command failed: benchmark targeted crate arkama integration test requiring OpenSSL headers unavailable in environment.

name: Arkama core download loop performance + correctness

description: Reset benchmark to arkama_core local e2e payload test; switched workspace reqwest to rustls-only (disable default features) to avoid OpenSSL dependency and establish runnable baseline.
Tried one-time seek per stream (remove per-chunk seek) + O(1) segment state update fast-path + SlowestTracker duplicate-duration fix; no primary metric gain on download_segmented_large_payload.
Sanity rerun with no code changes to gauge metric variance; lower score appears to be warm-cache noise, so baseline kept unchanged.

name: Arkama core download median-of-3 performance + correctness

description: Stabilized benchmark signal: autoresearch.sh now runs download_segmented_large_payload 3x and uses median result; re-baselined after measurement methodology update.
Batched segmented state-sync updates (64KiB) plus update_state id-index fast path to reduce mutex churn; measured median regressed by ~1ms and introduced unused-assignment warnings.
Tried one-time seek per stream (remove per-chunk seek in segmented/single loops). Median regressed significantly on local segmented payload benchmark.

name: Arkama core segmented download throughput (6x loop) + correctness

description: Amplified benchmark signal by running download_segmented_large_payload six downloads per test run (still median-of-3 in script); re-baselined for lower jitter.
Reduced segmented hot-path mutex churn by batching resume-state updates to 64KiB and adding direct id-index fast path in update_state while flushing pending state on stop/error/recycle boundaries.
Tuned state-sync batch size from 64KiB to 256KiB. Reduced lock frequency further but benchmark regressed versus kept 64KiB variant.
Tuned state-sync batch size from 64KiB to 128KiB. Better than 256KiB but still slower than kept 64KiB variant.
Tuned state-sync batch size from 64KiB to 32KiB. Higher update frequency increased contention and regressed benchmark.
Removed unnecessary read permissions from output file open options (prepare_output + async segment/single writers). No primary metric improvement versus kept code.
Skipped per-chunk atomic progress accounting when no event subscribers are present to reduce contention, but benchmark still regressed versus kept variant.
Attempted correctness fix for SlowestTracker duplicate durations (replace BTreeSet with duplicate-aware sample vector + tests). No primary metric improvement on current workload.
Tried state persistence IO optimization: compact JSON serialization and skipping immediate first periodic-save tick (initial state already written). Benchmark regressed on current workload.
No-code-change sanity run showed high variance on current cargo-driven benchmark path; discarded to avoid treating ambient load noise as a regression/improvement.
Removed redundant ensure_parent_dir calls from hot inner loops (segmented/single) and perform parent-dir creation once before download loops; keeps behavior and reduces repeated filesystem checks.
Avoid redundant immediate periodic state save tick (`tokio::time::interval` first tick) since execute path already performs explicit initial save_state before workers start.

Correctness attempt: make SlowestTracker duplicate-aware via `(Duration, marker)` BTreeSet keys and add duplicate-duration tests. Result did not show convincing primary improvement and likely adds overhead; discarded for now.
Precomputed emit_progress once and skipped per-chunk atomic/event work when no subscribers. Result not convincing on noisy run and did not beat established 316ms level.
Refactored response consumption from `bytes_stream().next()` to `Response::chunk()` in segmented/single loops to reduce stream wrapper overhead. No primary gain.

name: Arkama core segmented throughput (direct test binary) + correctness

description: Rebased benchmark harness to execute built `download_e2e` test binary directly (same workload, median-of-3), reducing cargo command overhead noise and establishing new baseline.
Tried skipping per-chunk atomic progress accounting/event dispatch when there are no subscribers by precomputing emit_progress. Regressed on direct-binary benchmark.
Retested segmented one-time seek (seek once before stream write, no per-chunk seek). Large regression on direct-binary benchmark, confirming previous result.
Tried compact state serialization (`serde_json::to_vec`) instead of pretty JSON in save_state. Regressed on direct-binary benchmark.

name: Arkama core segmented throughput (direct binary, warmup, median-of-5) + correctness

description: Further stabilized benchmark: direct test binary now uses one warm-up run and median-of-5 measured runs to reduce jitter and overfitting risk.
Retested no-subscriber progress shortcut (precompute emit_progress, skip atomic/send_event when absent) under warmup+median-of-5 harness; still regressed.
Tuned segmented state-sync batch threshold from 64KiB to 96KiB, reducing mutex update frequency while preserving resume fidelity boundaries.
Follow-up tuning: 112KiB state-sync batch threshold. Regressed vs kept 96KiB setting.
Further tuned segmented state-sync batch threshold to 88KiB; reduced lock/update overhead while retaining periodic flush semantics, yielding stronger median performance.
No-change validation rerun after 88KiB keep: observed higher median (155ms), indicating substantial environment variance; keep retained but confidence reduced.
A/B check against kept 88KiB: reverting batch size to 96KiB produced baseline-level median and did not outperform current best.
No-change calibration run on current head; tiny median shift confirms residual jitter around 150ms band.
Tried optimistic non-blocking state sync (`try_lock`) at batch boundaries to reduce hot-path await contention, with forced async flush on boundaries. No primary gain.
Removed unnecessary read access flags from output file open paths (prepare_output + segmented/single writers), keeping write-only intent and slightly reducing open-path overhead.
Retested compact state serialization (`serde_json::to_vec`) atop current head; no primary improvement under stabilized harness.
No-change calibration run on current head; median remains around 149-150ms, indicating recent keep is within observed variance but directionally better than 153ms baseline.
Batch threshold sweep: 80KiB increased state update frequency and did not outperform kept 88KiB setting.
Batch threshold sweep: 92KiB delivered no improvement versus kept 88KiB in current harness.
